newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian castorseed eases, overseas buying sluggish.
newsitem.headline: Indian castorseed eases, overseas buying sluggish.

text.p: Castorseed June delivery dropped further to 1,092/1,093 rupees per quintal from 1,101/1,102 rupees on the back of fresh speculative selling, floor sources said.

Sluggish overseas buying and continued pressure of arrivals prompted fresh offerings by the bear operators while bulls remained silent. Daily average arrivals of castorseed in the Gujarat region remained higher at 25,000/30,000 bags (75 kg each).
"Reports of bright crop prospects in Brazil and China also softened market sentiment here," said Dilip Thakkar, a leading operator.
Meanwhile in Bombay traders indicated castorseed September delivery at 1,170/1,175 rupees per quintal but no trading took place.
Groundnut oil slid to 355/356 rupees per 10 kg from 358/360 rupees per 10 kg amid sluggish physical demand and increased arrivals of imported edible oils at Bombay port.
"We are expecting arrivals of about 25,000/30,000 tonnes of imported edible oils including palm oil and sunflower oil at Bombay port in the current week," one miller said.
Imported palm oil was steady at 282/283 rupees per 10 kg, as was imported sunflower oil at 262/263 rupees per 10 kg. In Rajkot spot groundnut oil was steady at 560/565 rupees per 15 kg.
